328	### The Station-Gain Account (Invented 1905)
329	Teague created the "station-gain" line to track accounting reality:
330	- One side: butterfat credited to patrons on station's test (what the station books said it bought)
331	- Other side: butterfat actually received at Larrow Green in cream (what they actually had)
332	- The second was always larger by 5.25 percent
333	
334	**1898 entry (example):**
335	- Credited to patrons: 57,760 lb
336	- Received at Larrow Green: 60,800 lb
337	- Station gain: 3,040 lb (five and a quarter percent)
338	- Entry phrase: "as usual" (which stopped anyone looking)
339	
340	**Why invented:** "A difference that will not be entered somewhere will come back and bite you at audit"
341	
342	### Teague's Theory on Arrangement
343	Testimony to board of arbitration (and repeated in 1948):
344	> Cream is portable, and that station was in one pair of hands for twenty-nine seasons. One man weighed the milk, one man drew the sample, one man made the test, one man wrote the figure that the pay slip was made from, and one man ran the separator. There was no second man in that building from the spring to the fall. I do not say what any particular person did on any particular day, because I was not there and I do not know. I say that a business which is arranged so that a single man can take a little and write down a little less is a business that will sooner or later have a little taken from it, and that no set of books ever made can prevent it. The remedy is two men or a lock, and the Association had neither.
